The figure above shows the graphs of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x).$ Evaluate ${lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{f(x)+2g(x)}{1+xg(x)}.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{f(x)+2g(x)}{1+xg(x)}=\frac{{lim}_{x\to \,2}(f(x)+2g(x))}{{lim}_{x\to \,2}(1+xg(x))}.
$$

We find from the graph that  ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=6$  and ${lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)=2.$ Calculating the limits of the numerator and denominator separately, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}(f(x)+2g(x))=6+2(2)=10
$$

and

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}(1+xg(x))=1+2(2)=5.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{f(x)+2g(x)}{1+xg(x)}=\frac{10}{5}=2.\end{aligned}
$$
